blocks.md: Geographers use **graphs** to show data clearly. A **bar graph** compares quantities in separate groups (for example crop production by region). A **line graph** shows change over time (for example monthly temperature). A **pie chart** shows how a total is divided: the whole circle is 360°. Every graph needs a **title**, **labels** on the axes, a suitable **scale** and **units**.

blocks.title: Pie chart angles
blocks.md: Angle for a category = (value ÷ total) × 360°. Example: if cassava is 40 tonnes of a total of 200 tonnes, its angle is 40 ÷ 200 × 360 = **72°**. Check that all angles add up to 360° before drawing with a protractor.

blocks.title: Climate graph
blocks.md: A climate graph shows **temperature** as a line and **rainfall** as bars for each month. Read: (1) the highest and lowest monthly temperature and the **annual range** (highest − lowest); (2) the rainy months and the dry months; (3) the annual rainfall (add the monthly bars); then describe the climate. A hot place with rain all year is equatorial; hot with a long dry season is tropical.

**Photographs and sketches.** To interpret a photograph, say what is in the **foreground** (near), **middle ground** and **background** (far), name features (relief, vegetation, buildings, rivers, farming), say what they show about the area (climate, human activities) and add a short sketch with labels. Always describe what you can see before explaining why.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not start a vertical scale in the middle: begin at zero for bar graphs.
- Pie chart angles must add up to 360°.
- Describing a photograph is not the same as inventing facts: write only what the picture shows.

blocks.title: Example 1: pie chart angle
blocks.statement: In a village, 30 of the 120 families grow coffee. What angle represents coffee on a pie chart?
steps: Check: the other categories must give 270°.

blocks.title: Example 2: annual range
blocks.statement: A town has a hottest month of 29 °C and a coolest month of 24 °C. What is the annual temperature range?
steps: A small range is typical near the Equator.
